title: Factor Sorting Challenge
description: Classify 12 different resources into the four factors of production (land, labor, capital, entrepreneurship) through an interactive drag-and-drop challenge that tests understanding of economic resource categories.
learning_objectives: Correctly identify which resources belong to each factor of production category
Distinguish between natural resources (land), human effort (labor), tools (capital), and innovation (entrepreneurship)
Understand that some resources might appear ambiguous but have clear economic classifications
Recognize real-world examples of each factor across different industries
instructions: Review the 12 resource items displayed in the sorting area
Drag each resource to the correct factor of production category (Land, Labor, Capital, or Entrepreneurship)
Consider the economic definition of each factor before placing items
Click 'Check Answers' to see which classifications are correct
Review any incorrect answers and understand the proper classification
materials_needed: Drag-and-drop interface with four drop zones

items_to_sort.explanation: Fishing rights are access to a natural resource (fish in the ocean), making this a land factor
Human-made equipment used in production is capital, not land
Human mental effort and skills are labor, even for highly skilled workers
Innovation, risk-taking, and organizing other factors is entrepreneurship
Oil is a natural resource extracted from the earth, categorized as land
Vehicles used for business production are capital equipment
Skilled healthcare workers provide labor through their physical and mental effort
The act of starting a business involves entrepreneurial risk and organization
Sunlight is a natural resource provided by nature, not created by humans
Point-of-sale systems are human-made tools used in business operations
Management skills and knowledge are human capital, a form of labor
Taking on risk is a defining characteristic of entrepreneurship

perfect.message: Perfect! You've mastered identifying factors of production.

strong.message: Great work! You understand most factor classifications.

needs_review.message: Good effort. Review the red items and try again.

needs_help.message: Review factor definitions and try again. Ask for help if needed.

common_mistakes.correction: Robots are capital - human-made tools. Labor requires human effort.
Management skills are labor (human capital). Entrepreneurship is specifically about risk-taking and organizing a business.

common_mistakes.mistake: Classifying starting a business as capital
common_mistakes.correction: The act of starting a business is entrepreneurship. Capital refers to the physical equipment purchased.

deliverables: Correctly sorted all 12 resources into proper factor categories
Understanding of why each resource belongs to its specific factor
Ability to distinguish between similar-seeming factors (labor vs entrepreneurship, land vs capital)

criteria: Correctly identified all land resources (natural resources)
Correctly identified all labor resources (human effort)
Correctly identified all capital resources (human-made tools)
Correctly identified all entrepreneurship resources (innovation and risk)

teacher_notes: Students commonly confuse labor with entrepreneurship (both involve people) and land with capital (both can be physical). Emphasize that labor is ANY human effort, entrepreneurship is specifically organizing/risk-taking, land is NATURAL resources, and capital is HUMAN-MADE tools. The drag-and-drop immediate feedback helps reinforce correct classifications.
